schema: Each site: slug (data file names), name, region, country, club/clubShort/source (whose site guide the metadata comes from), lat/lon of take-off (WGS84), takeoffAmsl_ft, relief_ft, windFrom [from°, to°] working arc (clockwise), strengthBand_mph, workingWind, character, hazards. Terrain/landcover per slug under data/terrain and data/landcover (scripts/fetch-terrain.mjs, scripts/fetch-surface.mjs).

sites.name: Devil's Dyke
sites.character: Half-mile NW ridge leading to a north-facing bowl with a NE spur, then a 2-mile north ridge toward Truleigh Hill. One of the classic South Downs sites.
sites.hazards: Sea-breeze can encroach from behind the hill causing abrupt, severe turbulence. In NNE the take-off sits in wind-shadow with rotor at the rear of the paddock. Westerlies give very turbulent air off the bowls; the valley behind take-off holds rotor and sink.

sites.name: Firle
sites.character: North-facing bowl giving on to the northerly Firle ridge. A friendly, popular training-friendly site in the right conditions.
sites.hazards: Trees on the slope generate turbulence and dangerous sink near the fence. Steep wind gradient on take-off. Bowl geometry creates a venturi — wind can appear more aligned than it is, with serious rotor low in the bowl when off-axis, especially strong NE.

sites.name: Mount Caburn
sites.character: South-west facing dome with a bowl beyond, standing free 2 km SE of Lewes. A distinctive isolated hill with a small but reliable lift band.
sites.hazards: Often roughened by the sea breeze. Severe rotor behind the western ridge — carry ample height. Wind accelerates around the south/east sides; venturi in the bowl can produce 180° shifts over the landing field.

sites.name: Beachy Head
sites.character: South-east facing bowl with additional SSE-facing chalk cliffs above the sea, 2 miles SW of Eastbourne.
sites.hazards: Serious turbulence when lapse rates are poor, especially in summer. Dangerous rotor behind the cliffs in southerly winds. No safe bottom landing below the main cliffs — slippery rocks and limited beach.

sites.name: Ditchling Beacon
sites.character: North-facing bowl with ridges running 7 km east to Offham and 2 km west to the Clayton windmills. One of the highest points on the South Downs.
sites.hazards: Trees on the lower slopes create a steep wind gradient with lee turbulence. Strong winds produce rotor behind the trig point; NE winds can give site-wide rotor on the eastern side.

sites.name: Bo Peep
sites.character: North-east ridge system with multiple bowls running west to a 700 ft trig point, and a northerly ridge past Firle. Superb soaring potential along the extended ridge.
sites.hazards: Trees in front of the Bostal Down launch give severe turbulence in strong winds. Marked venturi in the quarry distorts wind assessment; rotor behind the quarry in NNE.

sites.name: High & Over
sites.character: A small, steep, tree-covered bowl facing due east over the Cuckmere river valley, south of Alfriston.
sites.hazards: A fully recirculating rotor can set up over the car park. Fast changes in wind direction and strength with gusty thermals. Often sink over the trees in the bowl. Not a site for inexperienced pilots.

sites.name: Newhaven Cliffs
sites.character: South-facing and SSW chalk sea-cliff runs. Coastal soaring where lift depends on the air–sea temperature differential as much as wind strength.
sites.hazards: Rotor behind the cliff for almost its full extent where the land slopes away. Venturi and wind-shadow at the point in easterly components. The airflow at Brighton Marina is very turbulent — stay clear of the eastern arm.
